sentences.text: My name is Emily,
and I'm so happy to have you here with me today.
In today's episode,
we're going to talk about the weather.
Talking about the weather
is a very common conversation topic in English.
Whether you're talking to a friend,
a coworker, or even a stranger,
knowing how to discuss the weather is important.
In this episode, we will learn important vocabulary,
useful phrases, and how to ask and answer questions
about the weather in English.
Let's get started.
Part one, common weather vocabulary.
First, let's go over some common words
related to the weather.
I will say each word slowly,
and you can repeat after me.
Weather, the condition of the atmosphere,
including temperature, rain, wind, and clouds.
Temperature, how hot or cold it is outside.
Rain, water falling from the sky and drops.
Snow, frozen water that falls from the sky and white flakes.
Cloudy, when the sky is covered with clouds.
Sunny, when there is a lot of sunlight.
Windy, when the wind is strong.
Foggy, when it is difficult to see
because of thick mist in the air.
Thunderstorm, a storm with lightning, thunder, and rain.
Cold, when the temperature is low.
Hot, when the temperature is high.
Warm, when the temperature is comfortable,
neither too hot nor too cold.
Part two, useful phrases for talking about the weather.
Now, let's learn some useful phrases
to talk about the weather.
I will say each phrase twice.
Listen carefully and repeat after me.
What's the weather like today?
A common question to ask about the weather.
It's sunny today.
When the sun is shining and there are no clouds,
it's cloudy today.
When there are many clouds in the sky,
but it's not raining, it's raining.
When water is falling from the sky,
it's snowing.
When frozen water is falling from the sky,
it's very windy today.
When there is a strong wind, it's hot outside.
When the temperature is very high, it's cold today.
When the temperature is very low,
the weather is nice today.
When the weather is good and comfortable,
it's a little chilly.
When the temperature is a bit cold, but not too much.
Part three, asking about the weather.
In this part, we'll talk about how to ask questions
about the weather.
Here are some examples.
Listen carefully and repeat after me.
What's the temperature today?
To ask about how hot or cold it is.
Is it going to rain today?
To ask if rain is expected?
Will it snow this week?
To ask if snow is expected in the future?
Is it going to be sunny tomorrow?
To ask if the sun will be shining the next day?
How's the weather where you are?
To ask someone about the weather in their location.
Part four, talking about future weather.
It's also common to talk about the weather in the future.
Here are some sentences that can help you do that.
It's going to rain tomorrow.
To talk about rain that will happen in the future.
The weather will be sunny this weekend.
To talk about sunny weather in the future.
It looks like it will snow next week.
To predict snow in the future.
It's going to be windy later today.
To talk about wind that will happen later.
Tomorrow's weather is going to be cold.
To talk about cold weather expected tomorrow.
Part five, common situations to talk about the weather.
Let's now look at some situations when you might talk about the weather.
I will give you some examples of situations and what you can say.
When you are meeting a friend in the morning.
Good morning.
It's a beautiful day today, isn't it?
Wow, it's so cold today.
Do you have a jacket?
When you're at work and talking to a coworker.
Did you hear?
It's going to rain this afternoon.
I'm so glad it's sunny today.
It's been cloudy for days.
When you're talking to a stranger or a neighbor.
The weather is nice today, isn't it?
I hope it doesn't snow tomorrow.
I need to drive to work.
When you're making plans with someone.
Let's go to the park tomorrow if the weather is nice.
We should stay inside if it's going to rain all day.
Part six, common problems and complaints about the weather.
Sometimes the weather isn't perfect.
Here are some common problems people talk about when the weather is bad.
It's too hot today.
When the temperature is uncomfortably high.
It's so cold outside.
When the temperature is very low, I don't like the rain.
When it's raining and you don't want it, the weather is so unpredictable.
When the weather changes quickly, it's so foggy this morning.
When you can't see clearly because of fog.
Part seven, summary and practice.
Great job.
Let's review everything we've learned today.
Important words, weather, temperature, rain, snow, cloudy, sunny, windy, foggy,
thunderstorm, hot, cold, warm.
Useful phrases.
What's the weather like today?
It's sunny today.
It's snowing.
The weather is nice today.
Questions about the weather.
What's the temperature today?
Is it going to rain today?
Will it snow this week?
Future weather.
It's going to rain tomorrow.
The weather will be sunny this weekend.
It looks like it will snow next week.
Common situations.
Talking to a friend, coworker, stranger or neighbor about the weather.
Common problems.
Too hot, too cold, rain, fog, unpredictable weather.
Now try to practice these phrases.
Imagine you are talking about the weather with a friend or coworker.
You can listen to this episode again to improve your pronunciation and confidence.
